Demand for declaration of a National holiday on the birth anniversaries of
Bhagwan Rushabhdev and Bhagwan Mahavir Ji
DR. K. LAXMAN (Uttar Pradesh): Thank you, Mr. Deputy Chairman, Sir, for giving
me this opportunity to raise the most sentimental and emotive issue pertaining not
only to the Jain community but also to all the peace lovers of this country. जैन धमर् के

का जन्म पिवतर् अयोध्या म(cid:514) हुआ था। जैन धमर् के आिखरी व 24व(cid:514) तीथ(cid:522)कर भगवान महावीर जी थे।
तीथ(cid:522)कर जो होते ह(cid:517), वे ससं ार और सागर, जन्म मरण के चकर् से मोक्ष तक का माग र् िदखाते ह(cid:517)।
तीथ(cid:522)कर कम(cid:537) से मु(cid:426) होकर कै व(cid:202)य ज्ञान (cid:290)ा(cid:195)त करते ह(cid:517)। ऐसे दो महानुभाव भगवान के रूप म(cid:514),
भागवान ऋषभदेव जी और भगवान महावीर जी, these two exemplary and extraordinary
figures, shaped the ethical and spiritual landscape of not only Jainism but also of the
broader cultural fabric of our great nation.
Bhagwan Rishabhdev, the first Tirthankara, is widely regarded as the founding
figure of Jain philosophy. His teachings are based on the principles of non-violence
th
means ahimsa and satya means truth. Bhagwan Mahavir ji, the 24 Tirthankara,
further refined and deepened these teachings which are integral to the path of spiritual
enlightenment and peace. His life and teachings, cutting across religious boundaries,
offer universal values that are relevant to the humanity. The Jain community for
centuries has made immeasurable contribution to the growth and progress of India
whether in the field of business, trade, education, philanthropy and social welfare.
Their efforts in promoting sustainability, charity and non-violence have played a vital
role in shaping harmonious, prosperous and inclusive society. We have seen their
yeoman service, particularly during the corona period. We have seen how dedicated
they are to the needs of society. In recognition of the contribution of these two
profound spiritual figures, Bhagwan Rishabhdev ji and Bhagwan Mahavir ji, I urge
upon the Government to declare their birth anniversaries as national holidays and see
that the sentiments of not only the Jain community but of all the peace-loving people
are honoured. Thank you very much, Sir.
